title: Invariant-affine construction of a finite quotient from an ample source
statement: Let B and V be Noetherian schemes [pqf-def-locnoeth], p:V→B locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], L an absolutely ample invertible module on V [def-sc-invertible-module, def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module], and H a finite group acting on V over B. There exist a scheme Q and morphisms q:V→Q and r:Q→B with qr=p such that q is an admissible finite scheme quotient [def-per-admissible-finite-scheme-quotient], surjective and categorical among all schemes, with nonempty actual geometric pullbacks on which the induced H action is transitive. The morphism r is locally of finite type. Restricting q to every H-invariant open U gives its admissible finite categorical quotient onto an open W of Q with q^-1(W)=U. This includes non-quasi-compact invariant opens. No quasi-projectivity, projectivity, ampleness or integrality assertion about Q is included.

proof.text: Each orbit is finite. The ample finite-principal-affine theorem encloses it in an affine open inside any specified invariant open. Apply invariant affine shrinking to the action groupoid, whose arrows are the disjoint union of H copies of V. Its source and target are finite locally free: on the components they are identities and automorphisms. Thus invariant affine opens cover V and refine every invariant open, including inverse images of base affine opens.

source.place: Rydh Theorem 4.4 and Proposition 4.7; original quotient steps 2--7

proof.text: On each invariant W=Spec A form C=A^H. The monic polynomial product_h(T-h(a)) shows each a integral over C. Over an affine T=Spec R of B with W⊆p^-1(T), the affine-pairs finite-type criterion makes A finite type over R. The same generators generate over C, so integral finite generation makes A finite as a C-module. Artin--Tate over the Noetherian R makes C finite type over R.

source.place: Rydh Theorem 4.4 and Proposition 4.7; original quotient steps 2--7

proof.text: The affine-groupoid orbit-fibres theorem gives surjectivity and orbit fibres for Spec A→Spec C, including over each algebraically closed field. A point of the geometric pullback is a rational point: its residue field is algebraic over the algebraically closed field because this morphism is finite. Thus the theorem on field-valued points gives transitivity on the actual pullback carrier, using the maps induced by each a_h and the pullback universal property. The integral spectrum map is closed, hence a topological quotient.

source.place: Rydh Theorem 4.4 and Proposition 4.7; original quotient steps 2--7

proof.text: For f∈C prove C_f=(A_f)^H. Injectivity follows from the zero-fraction criterion. For a fixed fraction a/f^r, choose for each h an exponent killing h(a)-a. Their maximum works for every h, so f^n*a∈C represents the same fraction. This argument includes zero divisors, nilpotent f and zero rings. These identifications commute with restriction and identify the invariant sheaf with O_Spec(C) on the distinguished-open basis and hence on all opens.

source.place: Rydh Theorem 4.4 and Proposition 4.7; original quotient steps 2--7

proof.text: On the topological orbit space |V|/H put the sheaf of invariant sections. The images of invariant affine opens are open, with inverse image exactly W. Steps 3--4 identify the restrictions with Spec C. The identifications on overlaps are the identity on the common invariant sheaf, so the cocycle condition holds. Glue these charts to Q and the local ring maps to q. Finiteness is local on the target, hence q is finite and surjective, with the orbit topology, orbit fibres and sectionwise invariant-sheaf formula.

source.place: Rydh Theorem 4.4 and Proposition 4.7; original quotient steps 2--7

proof.text: An invariant morphism V→Z factors continuously through the orbit topology. On every open of Z its pullback on sections is fixed and therefore factors uniquely through the invariant sheaf. The resulting ringed-space map is local: for a point of Q choose a point above it; the image of a nonunit germ in O_Z is a nonunit upstairs, so cannot be a unit downstairs. This gives the unique scheme morphism Q→Z. Apply it to p to obtain r and q r=p.

source.place: Rydh Theorem 4.4 and Proposition 4.7; original quotient steps 2--7

proof.text: The affine charts in Step 2 cover each r^-1(T), proving r locally of finite type. For any invariant open U, its image W in Q is open and q^-1(W)=U. Restrict the action and the same invariant sheaf. Step 1 gives its affine charts even when U is not quasi-compact. The same arguments prove the admissible finite quotient and categorical assertions for q_U:U→W.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_finiteGroup_quotient_of_ample
    (B V : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian B] [IsNoetherian V]
    (p : V ⟶ B) [LocallyOfFiniteType p]
    (L : V.Modules) [L.IsInvertible] (hL : Scheme.Modules.IsAmple V L)
    (H : Type v) [Group H] [Finite H] (a : H →* Aut V)
    (ha : ∀ h : H, (a h).hom ≫ p = p) :
    ∃ (Q : Scheme.{u}) (r : Q ⟶ B) (q : V ⟶ Q),
      q ≫ r = p ∧ IsAdmissibleFiniteSchemeQuotient a q ∧ Surjective q ∧
      (∀ (Ω : Type u) [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω] (t : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ Q),
        Nonempty ↥(pullback (C := Scheme.{u}) q t) ∧
        ∀ x y : ↥(pullback (C := Scheme.{u}) q t),
          ∃ (h : H) (l : pullback q t ⟶ pullback q t),
            l ≫ pullback.fst q t = pullback.fst q t ≫ (a h).hom ∧
            l ≫ pullback.snd q t = pullback.snd q t ∧ l x = y) ∧
      (∀ (Z : Scheme.{u}) (f : V ⟶ Z), (∀ h : H, (a h).hom ≫ f = f) →
        ∃! g : Q ⟶ Z, q ≫ g = f) ∧
      LocallyOfFiniteType r ∧
      ∀ U : V.Opens, (∀ h : H, (a h).hom ⁻¹ᵁ U = U) →
        ∃ (W : Q.Opens) (aU : H →* Aut U.toScheme) (qU : U.toScheme ⟶ W.toScheme),
          q ⁻¹ᵁ W = U ∧
          (∀ h : H, (aU h).hom ≫ U.ι = U.ι ≫ (a h).hom) ∧
          qU ≫ W.ι = U.ι ≫ q ∧ IsAdmissibleFiniteSchemeQuotient aU qU ∧
          ∀ (Z : Scheme.{u}) (f : U.toScheme ⟶ Z),
            (∀ h : H, (aU h).hom ≫ f = f) →
              ∃! g : W.toScheme ⟶ Z, qU ≫ g = f
